style_sentence: Stylized comic-book 3D game model with a cel-shaded look: flat bright saturated colours in clean hard-edged areas, bold simple shapes, no gradients, no fine texture detail, even front lighting with no cast shadows.
notes: Every prompt starts with the same style sentence. Thick black outlines and toon shading are added in code (as in the greybox), not painted into the textures, so they stay crisp at every size and angle.
floor and wall are built in code and are not in this list.
size_m is the height for characters and the longest edge for everything else.

Flick (thug_kicker) and Crusher (thug_crusher) now have their own models. Until their files are in public/assets, the game shows them as recoloured copies of the Sprat and Slab models. This takes the list to 10 entries (the original limit was 8).

busiest_moment.when: Wave 3: Volt, and 4 of Sprat, Flick, Slab and Crusher on screen (usually one of each), plus all props (1 dumpster, 3 crates, 2 trash cans, 2 street lamps).

triangles.note: The black outline draws each mesh a second time, so the triangle count doubles.

texture_memory.as_exported_2k: 9 base-colour maps x 22 MB = about 202 MB (about 605 MB if Tripo also exports normal and metal/roughness maps).
texture_memory.planned_at_load: Only the base colour is used, shrunk to 1024 for characters (5 x 5.6 MB) and 512 for props (4 x 1.4 MB) = about 34 MB. The 2k originals stay untouched in public/assets.

busiest_moment.phone_verdict: Yes. Triangles are unchanged (about 105k with the outline pass). Texture memory after shrinking goes from about 22 MB to about 34 MB, still safe for phones. Unshrunk 2k maps (about 202-605 MB) would not be.
